description: VS Code extension company building a streaming-first copilot: low-latency inline completions, multi-file context, per-dev quotas, and model/version pinning. Wants predictable latency for in-editor streaming and a partner for dedicated capacity if hosted cannot meet p99 SLOs.
notes:
Context: MantaFlow builds a commercial VS Code extension used by internal and external developer teams (SDKs, CLI). Primary value: instantaneous inline suggestions and multi-file refactor flows. Key asks: streaming completion with incremental token flushes, predictable p99 latency, robust model/version pinning, workspace-level rate limits, and SSO + audit logs.

UX/technical requirements (shorthand):
- streaming: incremental frames to editor, prefer sub-50ms p50 token latency, target p99 <60ms for single-token hops; observed hosted trial p95 ~48ms (see timeline).
- model pinning: pin to a quantized LLM for deterministic suggestions per-release; ability to roll back to previous model/version for regression testing.
- routing/fallback: want automatic fallback to lightweight local model or smaller hosted variant when capacity is constrained; graceful degrade to non-streaming batch completion if streaming capacity not available.
- rate limits: per-developer soft cap + org burst bucket; ability to throttle at workspace/plugin-level and surface quota info in extension UI.
- auth/keys: per-workspace API keys (team-managed), SAML SSO for org admins, rotate keys, tie to KMS for enterprise customers.
- telemetry & privacy: need audit logs for completions, retention policy 12 months by default, option for EU-only residency for some customers.
- infra: prefer VPC peering for Dedicated; open to hosted for early stages if SLOs met.
- caching: KV/prefix caching to reuse repeated completions, local ephemeral cache for offline edits.
- evals: inline suggestion quality gating & rollout canary in extension.

Quote from CTO: "We need streaming that feels instantaneous inside VS Code — if token RTT slips, the extension becomes unusable. Model pinning for release determinism is non-negotiable."

Concerns flagged: tokenization billing surprises from micro-interactions, rate-limit UX during peak refactors, and legal check on US/EU residency for enterprise beta.
